facts.text: Pagliacci premiered in Milan on 21 May 1892, conducted by Arturo Toscanini.
facts.evidence: Pagliacci premiered at the Teatro Dal Verme in Milan on 21 May 1892, conducted by Arturo Toscanini

facts.text: Critics were mixed at first, but the public loved Pagliacci instantly, and still does.
facts.evidence: Pagliacci received mixed critical reviews after its world premiere, but was instantly successful with the public and has remained so ever since.

facts.text: Leoncavallo, then little known, wrote Pagliacci after seeing the success of Mascagni’s Cavalleria rusticana.
evidence: Leoncavallo was a little-known composer when Pietro Mascagni's Cavalleria rusticana premiered
After seeing Mascagni's success, Leoncavallo decided to write an opera in response

facts.text: Leoncavallo said the story came from his childhood: the 1865 murder of a family servant, a case his father, a judge, investigated.
evidence: Leoncavallo claimed that he based the story of Pagliacci on an incident from his childhood: the 1865 murder of a Leoncavallo family servant
Leoncavallo's father, a judge, presided as magistrate over the criminal investigation

facts.text: The French author Catulle Mendès sued Leoncavallo for plagiarism; he later dropped the suit.
evidence: The French author Catulle Mendès sued Leoncavallo for plagiarism

facts.text: The Prologue was an afterthought: Leoncavallo wrote it to tempt the star baritone Victor Maurel into singing Tonio.
evidence: The opening Prologue was written for Maurel "as an afterthought"
as an inducement to a clever, but rather egotistical baritone to sing the part of Tonio

facts.text: Baritones often add a high A-flat and G near the end of the Prologue, though they aren’t in the original score.
facts.evidence: Towards the end of the prologue, singers often interpolate a high A♭ and a high G, although these do not appear in the original full score.

facts.text: In Leoncavallo’s manuscript, Tonio (not Canio) sings the last line, “La commedia è finita!” Canio took it over around 1895.
evidence: In the original manuscript, Tonio sang the opera's final line, "La Commedia è finita!"
The appropriation of this final line by Canio dates back to 1895.

facts.text: In 1907 Pagliacci became the first opera recorded complete, under Leoncavallo’s personal supervision.
facts.evidence: In 1907, Pagliacci was the first opera to be recorded in its entirety, with the Puerto Rican tenor Antonio Paoli as Canio and under Leoncavallo's personal supervision.

facts.text: The Met first paired Pagliacci with Cavalleria rusticana in a double bill on 22 December 1893.
facts.evidence: this time followed by Cavalleria rusticana on 22 December 1893

facts.text: Jean de Reszke sang Canio at the 1902 Paris Opera premiere, his last public performance.
facts.evidence: with legendary tenor Jean de Reszke as Canio in what would be his last public performance
